item.description: International Journal of Engineering — This study proposes a multi-objective framework for optimizing urban shortest paths by simultaneously considering traffic congestion and air quality. The objective is to minimize a weighted combination of travel time and pollutant exposure, with binary decision variables representing route selection. item.description: International Journal of Engineering — The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. item.description: International Journal of Technology in Education and Science — This research addresses the systemic educational inequality in Thailand, where a severe shortage of physical science laboratories in rural areas hinders the development of 21st-century scientific literacy. Using the ADDIE model, the study developed a virtual world technology innovation, the AR SciLab platform, to serve as a high-quality, risk-free learning infrastructure. item.description: PhilPapers (PhilPapers Foundation) — Segregation research increasingly measures who people encounter beyond home, yet physical mobility, place semantics, and digital activity are often combined without clear construct boundaries. item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — This research evaluates the socioeconomic feasibility of expanding the aerial cable car system in Manizales and Villamaría, Colombia, through a Social Cost-Benefit Analysis (SCBA). The assessment compares the three operational lines with a projected nine-line network, based on the Manizales Land Use Plan. item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Tourism in Goa is concentrated along the coastal belt, generating congestion, environmental stress, and uneven spatial development. This study develops a spatial decision-support framework to identify areas where tourism pressure should be contained and areas where diversification is more feasible. The analysis uses a 1 × 1 km grid across Goa and integrates tourism amenity indicators, environmental conditions, accessibility measures, and regulatory constraints. item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Accurate delineation of agricultural field boundaries is essential for agro-production monitoring, irrigation management, and sustainable land use planning. Manual digitization is labour-intensive and poorly scalable, while conventional segmentation algorithms are sensitive to spectral heterogeneity and weak inter-field contrast. The Zhetysai district of southern Kazakhstan – where approximately 45-50% of irrigated farmland exhibits salinization – exemplifies the urgent demand for automated field mapping. item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Cultural heritage is an important territorial resource for tourism development, yet the relationship between the distribution of listed heritage assets and tourism activity remains insufficiently understood. This study examines the geographical relationships between listed cultural heritage and tourism in Romania, focusing on territorial disparities and long-term changes. item.description: Geosport for Society — Women’s football is increasingly recognised as an important component of the sport tourism industry, with potential to diversify audiences, stimulate domestic travel, and advance gender inclusivity in emerging destinations. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Illegal trade in lobster pueruli (Benih Bening Lobster, BBL) presents interconnected challenges for fisheries governance, coastal livelihoods, and Indonesia’s maritime defense. This study examines how changes in BBL utilization policies, legal market access, and commodity traceability create potential vulnerabilities that may be exploited by smuggling networks. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Indonesia’s customs administration operates at the intersection of maritime mobility, trade facilitation, border protection, and revenue assurance, yet its risk systems are still primarily organized around declarations, manifests, entities, and transactions rather than the wider maritime operating picture. item.description: Journal Labor and Demographic economics — This article examines the relationship between ancestral knowledge, artisanal production, and socioeconomic benefits in Tabasco through an integrative review of academic literature and official documents. item.description: Applied Planetary Health — This study conducts a comparative analysis of socio-ecological vulnerability in six coastal communities of the Ecuadorian tropics, integrating mixed methods (quantitative and qualitative). The conceptual framework based on the components of Exposure, Sensitivity, and Adaptive Capacity allowed the construction of a Comparative Coastal Vulnerability Index (CCVI). item.description: International Journal of Research in English — Eco-feminism is an interdisciplinary intellectual and social movement that connects gender equality, environmental sustainability and social justice. It examines how systems of patriarchy, economic exploitation, unequal resource distribution and environmental degradation can reinforce one another. item.description: Journal of Ecological Engineering — Lateritic nickel mining can increase the transport of metal-bearing particles into river systems, where sediment–water partitioning governs metal mobility and ecological exposure. item.description: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University) — Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects African American women and contributes to racial health disparities in the United States. Although genetic susceptibility influences disease risk, growing evidence suggests that social determinants of health (SDOH), including neighborhood conditions, structural racism, and socioeconomic disadvantage, contribute to disease development and progression. item.title: Decolonizing ecocriticism: Climate justice, Indigenous knowledge, and more-than-human agency in contemporary Anglophone literature
item.description: International Journal of Research in English — Contemporary climate fiction increasingly challenges the assumption that ecological crisis can be understood exclusively through universalized narratives of environmental degradation. Such narratives often obscure the historical inequalities through which ecological harm is produced and unevenly distributed. This article proposes a decolonizing approach to ecocriticism through a comparative reading of Imbolo Mbue’s How Beautiful We Were (2021) and Amitav Ghosh’s Gun Island (2019). item.description: Preprint / source unavailable — Introduction: Community and public health systems face persistent fragmentation, inequitable access, and limited capacity to respond to evolving population health needs. These challenges are intensified by epidemiological transitions, social inequalities, and uneven access to preventive and primary healthcare. item.description: Urbanization, sustainability and society. — Purpose Connection and proximity to nature are associated with improved wellbeing outcomes. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Urban mobility faces simultaneous challenges of decarbonization and air quality improvement, requiring adaptive tools for planning and policy evaluation. This paper presents a digital twin (DT) framework that integrates agent-based modeling of personal and freight mobility with automatic calibration using real-time sensor and GPS data. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Cyberattacks on traffic signal systems pose growing risks to transport network resilience. Connected vehicles (CVs), through real-time communication and dynamic rerouting, may help mitigate these impacts, but their role under traffic signal attacks remains unclear. This paper investigates how transport network resilience changes under clustered and dispersed traffic signal attacks with different CV penetration rates. item.title: Measuring multidimensional housing pressure in equitable and resilient Australian cities
item.description: Discover Cities — Housing equity is central to resilient, inclusive and sustainable urban development. Yet housing policy is often framed narrowly around prices, rents, supply shortages or individual affordability stress. This paper develops the concept of common-good housing pressure to capture the spatial concentration of housing conditions that affect not only households, but also the wider functioning of cities. item.description: International Journal of Information Security — Federated learning (FL) enables multiple data holders to train machine learning models collaboratively without centralizing raw data, making it useful in privacy sensitive domains such as healthcare and institutional data sharing. FL keeps data local to clients while communicating only model updates, such as gradients or model deltas. item.description: Nano Convergence — Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are among the most promising energy conversion technologies for achieving sustainable and carbon-neutral energy systems. item.description: Research Square — Coupling satellite remote sensing with ground telemetry enhances urban exposure modeling, yet conventional random cross-validation substantially inflates predictive performance. We quantify spatial cross-validation inflation and evaluate mesoscale biophysical drivers across 13 regulatory air quality stations in the Kolkata-Howrah conurbation during 2024-2025. item.description: Research Square — Global pesticide use exceeded 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, and residues that persist beyond the treated field drive diffuse soil, surface water, and groundwater contamination linked to ecological harm and an estimated 150,000 pesticide poisoning deaths annually. item.description: Chapman & Hall/CRC eBooks — Geospatial data analysis has become an essential component of modern disaster management, providing spatially explicit information for hazard detection, risk assessment, early warning, emergency response, and post-disaster recovery. This chapter examines how geospatial data, machine learning, and artificial intelligence can be integrated to improve disaster preparedness and decision-making across multiple hazard contexts. item.description: Frontiers in Marine Science — Nearly four billion people depend on coastal ecosystems, where the growing influence of wildfire remains an understudied threat to ecosystem health. Wildfires alter watershed hydrology, mobilizing sediments, nutrients, and contaminants that degrade coastal water quality and disrupt marine habitats long after fires are extinguished. item.title: Ambient particulate chemical components and dengue incidence: A 10-year nationwide study in Thailand
item.description: PLoS ONE — Dengue remains a major public health concern in tropical regions, and environmental determinants are increasingly recognized as contributors to its transmission dynamics. Thailand experiences both recurrent dengue outbreaks and episodic air pollution; however, the role of particulate chemical components in dengue epidemiology remains unclear. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Urban logistics faces pressing challenges regarding climate goals, air pollution, and congestion. item.description: PLOS Climate — The COVID-19 lockdown created a natural experiment for examining how large changes in human activity coincided with urban air-quality change. item.description: Research Square — This study contributes to sustainable development research by examining the relationship between drought-related displacement and urban mobility patterns in Somalia. item.description: Big Earth Data — Population spatialisation serves as a critical nexus transforming aggregated population counts into spatially explicit population distributions, providing an essential foundation for urban planning, disaster management, and public health assessment. item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Despite the growing implementation of road pricing schemes globally, public acceptance remains a significant barrier. item.description: Scientific Reports — Natural disasters displace millions of people each year, and effective disaster response requires accurate models of population movement. item.description: Annals of Operations Research — With the increasing frequency and intensity of typhoon disasters, developing effective evacuation decision-making systems is critical for ensuring public safety. This paper proposes a data-driven approach that integrates machine learning (ML) classification models with system reliability evaluation to support typhoon evacuation operations. We address three key challenges: (1) predicting evacuation necessity based on meteorological data, (2) modeling uncertainty in evacuation networks, and (3) quantifying evacuation feasibility under resource constraints. item.description: Discover Hazards — Rising temperatures and climate change have intensified heat-related health risks, particularly in developing countries like India. Understanding the spatial distribution of heat-health risk is important for planning and mitigation. This study evaluates district-level Heat Health Risk Index (HHRI) patterns across Madhya Pradesh and Odisha, India. item.description: Journal of Edge Computing — Wildfires cause severe ecological and economic damage, and limiting it requires rapid and accurate detection. This study presents an image classification framework for wildfire detection in RGB images from the FLAME 3 dataset, captured by an unmanned aerial vehicle. The preprocessing pipeline applies gamma correction, sharpening, contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalisation (CLAHE) and class-balanced data augmentation. item.description: Earth system science data — Accurate aviation emission inventories provide the fundamental basis for environmental impact assessment, yet existing estimates typically rely on idealized trajectory assumptions and generic aircraft performance models. Here, we present a high-resolution, four-dimensional aviation emission inventory for purely domestic civil aviation flights within mainland China in 2023, built directly from onboard Quick Access Recorder (QAR) measurements covering 4.52 million flights (∼96.8 % of national commercial movements). item.description: Frontiers in Future Transportation — The purpose of this paper is to examine, from a bioethical perspective, the accessibility issues associated with the travel needs of families raising autistic children. item.description: Frontiers in Public Health — Introduction Air pollution is a major global public health challenge. Clean energy use is widely recognized as a key pathway to improving air quality and protecting public health. Against this backdrop, this study examines the impact of clean energy use on the health of farmers and herders in Xizang and its underlying mechanisms. item.title: De jure versus de facto lockdown measures and domestic violence: evidence from Italy
item.description: Economica — This paper investigates the impact of COVID‐19‐related restrictions on domestic violence in Italy, distinguishing between formal restrictions ( de jure ) and actual behavioural responses ( de facto mobility reduction). We assess how de jure and de facto lockdowns affected domestic violence incidence using a novel identification strategy that leverages the Oxford COVID‐19 Government Response Tracker's Stringency Index and reductions in traffic‐related air pollutants. item.title: The Economic Cost Of “Clean Air”: Evidence From The Air Pollution Prevention And Control Action Plan In China
item.description: Humanities and Social Sciences Communications — The Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan (APPCAP) is considered China’s largest initiative to combat air pollution. Despite its effectiveness in reducing haze pollution, there is limited empirical evidence on its economic impact. Employing a continuous difference-in-differences design, this paper evaluates the effect of the APPCAP on economic output between 2009 and 2017. item.title: The acoustic environment is structured more by place and fine particulate matter more by time across Rhode Island communities
item.description: Scientific Reports — Environmental comfort in cities is shaped by several exposures at once, yet noise and air pollution are often combined into a single index of environmental quality.
